questions_answered.is_destination_gpu_tensor_allocated_pers: No. The real probe allocates a fresh standalone scratch tensor (ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors_from_buft) for every promote/demote call and frees it before the process exits the mode. There is no persistent paired GPU backing kept around across calls in this prototype.
questions_answered.can_cpu_backing_be_released_after_promot: Yes, mechanically -- ggml_backend_buffer_free on the CPU-side scratch/tensor buffer is a real, working call (proven by cycle_stability.json: 50 alloc/copy/free cycles with flat external VRAM/RSS). But releasing llama_kv_cache's OWN cache_k_l{layer}/cache_v_l{layer} CPU buffer specifically is not exercised here -- see live_rebind_classification.
questions_answered.can_gpu_backing_be_released_after_demoti: Yes -- proven directly: cycle_stability.json shows external nvidia-smi VRAM returning to baseline after every one of 50 repeated GPU scratch alloc->copy->free cycles, and single_layer_promotion.json/pressure_test.json both show vram_after_scratch_free_mib dropping back toward vram_before_mib once the promotion scratch is freed.
questions_answered.does_kv_dev_override_allow_backing_owner: No. kv_dev_override (Phase 12B) only selects device at llama_context CONSTRUCTION time. llama_kv_cache::layers[il].k/.v are assigned once during context build and are never reassigned anywhere in llama-kv-cache.cpp afterward -- confirmed empirically by the poison test (see single_layer_promotion.json / single_layer_demotion.json): corrupting the promoted/demoted scratch copy has zero effect on generated tokens, meaning the live decode graph never reads it.
questions_answered.is_phase12c_limited_to_copying_between_p: Phase 12C is limited to copying REAL KV bytes into standalone scratch tensors on the destination device and verifying byte/hash equality. It is NOT limited to 'paired persistent tensors' in the sense of a pre-declared GPU mirror kept alive the whole time -- no such pairing exists in this prototype at all. The honest description is: one-shot, on-demand scratch-tensor copies, proven correct at the byte level, that the live decode graph does not consume.

explicit_tiering_disclosure: This is NOT tiering in the sense of Section 14's bar. No bytes are ever physically absent from a device while the graph is live and using that layer -- the ORIGINAL llama_kv_cache tensor for a layer stays exactly where kv_dev_override placed it at construction time for the entire lifetime of the context. What this prototype proves is a SEPARATE, freeable scratch copy on the other device, correct byte-for-byte, that the live decode graph ignores. Calling this 'tiering' would be dishonest; see live_rebind_classification below. Every promotion/demotion this phase performs produces a genuine duplicate (both the original tensor and the scratch copy resident simultaneously), never a move.
live_rebind_classification_evidence: Direct empirical falsification via poison test, not code-reading inference: after a byte-identical scratch copy is created on the destination device, the SAME scratch region is corrupted (0xAA-filled) in an independent fresh context before generation, and 8-token greedy generation output is compared byte-for-byte against an unpoisoned control run. In every promote/demote trial run (135M and 360M, ctx=2048 and ctx=200000, Q8_0 and Q5_1), poison_had_no_effect_on_output == true, meaning the live decode graph never reads the scratch/promoted copy. See single_layer_promotion.json, single_layer_demotion.json, pressure_test.json for the raw per-trial evidence.

ownership_state_machine.note: tools/membrane-kv-promotion-prefetch/ownership_state.{h,c} implements the IDEALIZED state machine (CPU_RESIDENT -> PROMOTING -> GPU_RESIDENT -> DEMOTING -> CPU_RESIDENT, ERROR on *_FAIL) described in Section 2/22, independent of what the real probe can currently deliver. It exists to make the bookkeeping/headroom logic testable in isolation (see tests/unit run of test_kv_ownership_state), NOT to claim the real probe achieves idealized ownership transfer. The real probe's demonstrated behavior is captured honestly above as classification B.
ownership_state_machine.duplicate_backing_during_transition_deta: PROMOTING and DEMOTING states hold group_bytes on BOTH sides simultaneously by design (cpu_bytes == gpu_bytes == group_bytes) -- this models the real probe's actual behavior honestly: every promote/demote call in this phase creates a genuine duplicate, never a move.
